$meta.title: Fluent 2 across the Power Platform
$meta.description: Structured guidance on how Fluent UI 2.0 (Fluent React v9) is used and themed across Power Apps (canvas modern controls), Power Pages, and PCF code components.
$meta.fluentVersion: Fluent 2 = Fluent UI React v9 (@fluentui/react-components); Fluent v8 = @fluentui/react (legacy)
$meta.confidence: High. The three items previously flagged as uncertain are now resolved against Microsoft Learn and the official microsoft/PowerApps-Samples source (see resolvedNotes).
resolvedNotes: PCF context.fluentDesignLanguage: tokenTheme is authoritative. Microsoft's own sample (microsoft/PowerApps-Samples component-framework/FluentThemingAPIControl) reads context.fluentDesignLanguage.tokenTheme; the '.theme' seen in some how-to prose is a documentation inconsistency. Use tokenTheme with optional chaining.
Power Pages Bootstrap: v3.3.6 AND v5 are supported; new sites are set up on v5, existing v3 sites can migrate (configure/bootstrap-overview).

PCF platform-library version drift is expected by design: you declare a version in the allowed range (Fluent v9 >=9.4.0 <=9.46.2) but the platform loads a higher one at runtime (9.68.0); React loads 17.0.2 model-driven / 16.14.0 canvas. This is documented, not an error.
$meta.officialMcpServers: There is no official Microsoft MCP server for Fluent 2 design tokens or theming. Two adjacent official MCPs are complementary: the Power BI Modeling MCP Server (TMDL/PBIP semantic-model edits + DAX; it does not generate visual theme JSON) and the Power Platform CLI built-in MCP (pac copilot mcp --run).

powerapps.title: Power Apps canvas — Modern controls & modern themes
powerapps.summary: Canvas apps ship 'modern controls' and 'modern themes' based on the Fluent 2 design system. Enabling the feature swaps the studio palette to Fluent-styled controls and unlocks a Themes pane that drives color, typography, borders and shadows from App.Theme.
powerapps.enableFeature: Open app > Settings > Updates > New > toggle 'Modern controls and themes' to On.
powerapps.controlsCount: 25 modern controls as of the modern-controls-reference (updated 2026-07-21). The set grows roughly monthly; verify against the reference.

Appearance maps to Fluent variants (Primary/Secondary/Outline/Subtle/Transparent). Key props: Text, Appearance, OnSelect.
Grouping surface for related content. Preview.

powerapps.fluentControlsNote: Mappings are conceptual (same Fluent 2 design language/behavior), not a literal 1:1 code re-export. The modern control set grows roughly monthly; verify against the modern-controls-reference and modern-control-updates docs. A standalone 'Icon' control appeared in earlier releases but is not in the current reference list; use the icon slot on modern controls or Fluent UI System Icons.

theming.howTo: Enable modern controls, open the Themes pane, then pick a built-in theme or Add a theme > Create custom theme (seed color, font, torsion, vibrancy, per-slot overrides) or Paste theme (YAML). Selecting a theme sets App.Theme and applies app-wide. A theme exposes a 16-slot brand color ramp, a Font, and a Name, reachable in Power Fx via App.Theme (e.g. Button.Fill = App.Theme.Colors.Primary).
theming.themeFormat: YAML (copy/paste from the Themes pane). Represented here as an object; required keys: Font, BasePaletteColor, HueTorsion, Vibrancy. ColorOverrides is optional.

themePropertyNotes.BasePaletteColor: Seed color (hex) used to generate all 16 slots.
themePropertyNotes.LockPrimaryColorPreview: Places seed in the middle slot; may break WCAG contrast. Leave off for accessibility-optimized ramp.

steps: Settings > Updates > New > turn on 'Modern controls and themes'.
Build the UI from the modern controls in the palette (classic controls move to Classic/Classic icons).
Open the Themes pane; select a built-in theme or create/paste a custom theme.
Confirm App.Theme is set; reference App.Theme.Colors.* in Power Fx for consistent color.
Test accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA) on desktop and mobile after theming.
gotchas: OnChange for Text/Number input fires on blur, not per keystroke; live-search logic must read the output property directly.
Applying a modern theme to classic controls only wires Power Fx variables; classic controls aren't Fluent v9 so won't look identical.
Once modern themes are on you can't pick classic themes (re-enable via Updates > Retired > Keep classic themes).
Built-in themes can't be edited or deleted; copy their YAML first. Deleting a custom theme referenced in Power Fx needs manual formula fixes.
Preview surface: controls and properties ship/change monthly.

modelDriven.title: Model-driven apps — the modern 'New Look' + modern theme overrides
modelDriven.summary: Model-driven apps modernize to Fluent 2 through the 'New Look'. Wave 1 (the refreshed look) is generally available and mandatory as of the 2026 release wave 1: makers can no longer revert to the classic look. Wave 2 (header and navigation refresh) is in public preview. This is the model-driven counterpart to canvas modern themes, and it is what a PCF control's context.fluentDesignLanguage inherits from in model-driven apps.

newLook.status: Wave 1 'The New Look' is GA and mandatory as of 2026 release wave 1 (no revert to classic). Wave 2 'header and navigation refresh' is public preview. Aligned to Fluent 2 and the foundation for future dark mode.

theming.summary: Classic theming is not honored under the New Look. Instead, supply a CustomTheme XML web resource referenced from an app setting; the platform generates the Fluent 2 ramp from your seed color, matching the canvas modern-theme model.
theming.mechanism: Create a web resource of type XML whose root is a <CustomTheme> element, then reference it via the app's theme app setting.

customThemeAttributes.basePaletteColor: Seed hex color the 16-slot ramp is generated from.
customThemeAttributes.lockPrimary: If true, pins the seed into the primary slot (can break WCAG contrast; leave off for an accessibility-optimized ramp).
customThemeAttributes.font: CSS font-family stack for the app.
customThemeAttributes.logoWebResource: Web resource name of the app logo (recommended 156x48 px).
customThemeAttributes.AppHeaderColors: Optional child element to theme the app header (background, foreground, backgroundHover/Pressed/Selected, etc.).

theming.customThemeExample: <CustomTheme basePaletteColor="#0f6cbd" vibrancy="0" hueTorsion="0" font="'Segoe UI', sans-serif" logoWebResource="contoso_company-logo" logoTooltip="Contoso" />
theming.notThemedYet: Some areas are not yet themed under the New Look (legacy grids, row summaries, focus view, sales pipeline).

modelDriven.pcfRelationship: A PCF (React/virtual) control in a model-driven app inherits this theme through context.fluentDesignLanguage.tokenTheme, exactly as it inherits canvas modern themes. See the pcf section.
gotchas: There is no toggle literally named 'Fluent 2'. Canvas uses the 'Modern controls and themes' toggle; model-driven uses the New Look (now mandatory) plus the header/navigation refresh (preview). Both are the Fluent 2 implementation.
Classic theme records are ignored under the New Look; migrate branding to a CustomTheme XML web resource + app setting.

powerpages.title: Power Pages — Bootstrap base + custom CSS with Fluent 2 tokens
powerpages.summary: Power Pages has no first-party Fluent 2 theme. Sites are built on Bootstrap with a Styling workspace (design studio). Achieve a Fluent 2 look by combining the Styling workspace brand kit with custom CSS that maps Bootstrap/site variables onto Fluent v9 design tokens exposed as CSS custom properties.
powerpages.approach: Bootstrap (v3.3.6 or v5) + Styling workspace brand kit + custom CSS defining Fluent 2 tokens as CSS variables and mapping Bootstrap onto them.

platform.bootstrap: Supports Bootstrap 3.3.6 and Bootstrap 5. New sites are set up on Bootstrap v5; existing v3 sites can migrate. Do not replace Bootstrap - some Power Pages scenarios depend on it.
platform.stylingWorkspace: 13 preset themes; per theme customize color palette (9 mapped colors + 3 user slots), background, font styles (basic fonts + 30+ Google Fonts), button styles, section margins. Brand kit = logo + palette + fonts.
platform.customCss: Upload via Styling > ... > Manage CSS (<= 1 MB). Files lower in the list take higher precedence. Editable in Visual Studio Code for the Web. The per-component paintbrush overrides Styling workspace and custom CSS unless !important is used.
platform.codeComponents: Standard PCF code components ARE supported in Power Pages: add a standard code component to a Dataverse form field (Data workspace form designer > + Component, or Portals Management > Basic Form Metadata > Control Style = Code Component), or embed with the Liquid tag {% codecomponent name:<namespace.Control> prop:'value' %}. Web client only. Not supported: React (virtual) controls + platform libraries (React controls don't re-render on other fields' changes), several Device.* APIs, Utility, uses-feature=true, and multi-field binding. So the Fluent-v9-via-platform-library path does not apply, but a standard control that bundles its own Fluent does work.

powerpages.fluentTokensNote: CSS variable names mirror Fluent v9's tokens object. Pull authoritative values from @fluentui/tokens (webLightTheme) instead of hardcoding. Default brand color is #0f6cbd; default font is Segoe UI.
powerpages.webComponentsOption: You can optionally load @fluentui/web-components (framework-agnostic Fluent 2 components) via CDN in a page/web template for real Fluent components on specific pages. This is NOT documented/supported for Power Pages - watch Content Security Policy and prefer the token-CSS approach for site-wide theming.
steps: In the design studio Styling workspace, set the brand palette to your Fluent ramp (seed #0f6cbd) and pick Segoe UI for headings/body.
Author a custom CSS file that declares Fluent 2 tokens as :root CSS variables.
Map Bootstrap/site selectors (e.g. .btn-primary, --bs-primary) onto the Fluent tokens.
Upload via Styling > ... > Manage CSS; order it below defaults so it wins on conflicts.
Preview across web/tablet/mobile; confirm the site's Bootstrap version before relying on version-specific CSS.
gotchas: Bootstrap version: v3.3.6 and v5 are both supported; new sites are on v5, existing v3 sites can migrate. Confirm the actual version before writing version-specific CSS.

PCF React (virtual) controls and platform libraries are NOT supported in Power Pages (React controls don't re-render on other fields' changes), so the Fluent-v9-via-platform-library path does not apply. Standard code components that bundle their own Fluent DO work (see platform.codeComponents).
Manage CSS precedence is bottom-wins; the paintbrush per-component styling overrides Styling workspace and custom CSS unless !important.
No fluentDesignLanguage bridge in Power Pages - you own the token values in CSS.

pcf.title: PCF code components — Fluent React v9 via platform libraries
pcf.summary: Build a React (virtual) PCF control that shares the host's React and Fluent v9 instances via platform libraries. This shrinks the bundle and makes the component pick up the host app's Fluent 2 theme automatically (canvas modern themes or model-driven refreshed look). Consume the host theme through context.fluentDesignLanguage.
pcf.scaffold: pac pcf init -n HelloFluent -ns SampleNamespace -t field -fw react -npm   (Power Platform CLI >= 1.37; -fw react creates a virtual React control)
pcf.manifestEssentials: Set control-type="virtual" on <control> (not standard). Add two <platform-library> children in <resources>: name="React" and name="Fluent". Remove the Fluent platform-library if you don't use Fluent. Fluent 8 and Fluent 9 cannot both be declared in one manifest.
pcf.manifestResourcesExample:
<resources>
  <code path="index.ts" order="1" />
  <platform-library name="React"  version="16.14.0" />
  <platform-library name="Fluent" version="9.46.2" />
</resources>
pcf.indexTsEssentials: React control lifecycle: init (no div parameter - React controls don't render DOM directly) > updateView (returns a React.ReactElement) > getOutputs > destroy. The platform renders the element returned by updateView.

properties.tokenTheme: Fluent v9 Theme tokens provided by the platform (use for FluentProvider theme).
properties.brand: BrandVariants the theme was generated from (use with createV8Theme for Fluent v8).
properties.isDarkTheme: boolean - whether the current theme is dark.

themingApi.detectEnabled: Any app: context.fluentDesignLanguage?.tokenTheme is truthy. Model-driven: context.appSettings.getIsFluentThemingEnabled().

pcf.fluentProviderPattern: With Fluent v9 controls + platform libraries the modern theme flows in automatically via the shared React context - often no FluentProvider is needed. To force a specific theme (or re-theme portaled components like menus/dialogs/tooltips), wrap the tree: <FluentProvider theme={context.fluentDesignLanguage.tokenTheme}>{/* control */}</FluentProvider>.
themingApproaches: Fluent v9 controls (easiest): add platform libraries; modern theme applies automatically via shared React context for non-portaled controls.
Fluent v8 controls: createV8Theme(context.fluentDesignLanguage.brand, context.fluentDesignLanguage.tokenTheme) from @fluentui/react-migration-v8-v9, then ThemeProvider.
Non-Fluent HTML: read tokens directly, e.g. style={{ fontSize: context.fluentDesignLanguage.tokenTheme.fontSizeBase300 }}.
Custom theme provider: wrap in your own FluentProvider when you want a different theme; or IdPrefixProvider with a custom idPrefix to opt out of modern theming.
steps: pac pcf init -n HelloFluent -ns SampleNamespace -t field -fw react -npm
npm install @fluentui/react-components (dev dependency; shared with the platform at runtime).
In ControlManifest.Input.xml set control-type="virtual" and add React + Fluent platform-library elements; declare input/output properties.
In index.ts implement init/updateView/getOutputs/destroy; return a Fluent component tree from updateView, wrapped in FluentProvider using context.fluentDesignLanguage.tokenTheme when present.
npm start to test in the harness; then package into a solution for canvas or model-driven apps (not Power Pages).
gotchas: context.fluentDesignLanguage.tokenTheme is authoritative for FluentProvider (verified in microsoft/PowerApps-Samples component-framework/FluentThemingAPIControl). The '.theme' seen in some how-to prose is a documentation inconsistency; prefer tokenTheme and use optional chaining.

Non-portaled v9 controls (Label, Button, Checkbox) inherit the modern theme automatically. Portaled v9 components (Combobox, Menu, Dialog, Tooltip) must be re-wrapped in a FluentProvider (and optionally IdPrefixProvider) or they lose theme tokens.
You can't convert a standard control to a virtual React control in place - scaffold fresh with -fw react.
Rebuild legacy virtual controls with CLI >= 1.37 for future React version upgrades.
React controls and platform libraries are not supported in Power Pages (standard code components are; see powerpages).
Platform library version drift is by design: the declared manifest version (Fluent v9 <=9.46.2) differs from the version loaded at runtime (9.68.0); React loads 17.0.2 model-driven / 16.14.0 canvas.
pcf.sampleRepo: microsoft/PowerApps-Samples > component-framework/FluentThemingAPIControl demonstrates four patterns: v9 theme inheritance, a custom v9 FluentProvider, the v8 createV8Theme bridge, and non-Fluent token use. https://github.com/microsoft/PowerApps-Samples/tree/master/component-framework/FluentThemingAPIControl

correctedMyths.note: Plausible-sounding claims about Fluent on Power Platform that are false. Check these before asserting that a Fluent generation applies to a surface — several of them are the difference between correct guidance and confidently wrong guidance.

items.myth: Power BI custom visuals use Fluent, so a Fluent 1 vs Fluent 2 choice is meaningful.
items.reality: No Fluent is shipped or referenced. powerbi-visuals-api 5.11.1 depends only on semver.

items.myth: Microsoft's Power BI visual samples demonstrate a Microsoft UI component library.
items.reality: Samples are pure D3. sampleBarChart uses d3-axis/d3-scale/d3-selection and no React.

items.myth: The Power BI theme JSON schema has a Fluent 1 and a Fluent 2 variant.
items.reality: Schema is version-independent. Only 'name' is required. The Fluent difference lives in the base theme.

items.myth: Power BI has only one default look, so there is nothing to switch.
items.reality: Three base themes exist: Fluent 2 (preview), Classic 2026, Classic 2018.

items.myth: Canvas classic controls are the Fluent 1 / @fluentui/react v8 controls.
items.reality: They are proprietary Power Apps controls. Docs state classic controls are not based on Fluent v9.

items.myth: PCF only supports Fluent 9, so Fluent 1 users are stuck.
items.reality: platform-library officially supports Fluent 8.29.0 and 8.121.1; Microsoft samples pin 8.121.1.

items.myth: You can declare both Fluent 8 and Fluent 9 platform libraries in one PCF manifest.
items.reality: Each is supported but they cannot both be specified in the same manifest.

items.myth: context.fluentDesignLanguage gives you v8 theme objects for Fluent 8 controls.
items.reality: The host emits only v9 tokens. Fluent 8 requires createV8Theme from @fluentui/react-migration-v8-v9.

items.myth: PCF React and platform libraries work in Power Pages.
items.reality: Verbatim FAQ answer is No. Canvas and model-driven apps only.

items.myth: Model-driven apps can be reverted to the classic Fluent 1 era look.
items.reality: New Look is mandatory as of 2026 Wave 1; makers cannot switch back. Classic theming is not honored.

items.myth: Power Pages uses Office UI Fabric Core or Fluent somewhere in its stack.
items.reality: It ships bootstrap.min.css, theme.css, portalbasictheme.css. No Fabric Core, no Fluent React.

items.myth: You can swap Bootstrap for a Fluent CSS library in Power Pages.
items.reality: Microsoft explicitly warns against it; some Power Pages scenarios depend on Bootstrap 3.3.x.

items.myth: ms-font-s / ms-font-m / ms-font-xl are the current Fabric Core type classes.
items.reality: Those are deprecated MDL2 classes. Canonical scale is ms-fontSize-10 through ms-fontSize-68.

items.myth: office-ui-fabric-core npm versions tagged fluent1 / fluent2 map to Fluent design generations.
items.reality: They are build-iteration prereleases; the series runs fluent5 through fluent9. Do not pin them.

fluentAppliesBySurface.fluent1Meaning: Nothing. No Fluent library is shipped, referenced or provided by the visuals SDK.
fluentAppliesBySurface.fluent2Meaning: Nothing. Host theming is host.colorPalette, not Fluent tokens.
fluentAppliesBySurface.guidanceToday: Do not offer a Fluent 1/2 choice. Theme via host.colorPalette / ISandboxExtendedColorPalette.

fluentAppliesBySurface.fluent1Meaning: No Fluent 1 theme exists. Nearest analogue is the Classic 2018 base theme.
fluentAppliesBySurface.guidanceToday: Map Fluent 1 to base theme Classic 2018 + #0078d4-era dataColors. Schema itself is versionless.

fluentAppliesBySurface.fluent1Meaning: Era-adjacent only. Classic controls are proprietary Power Apps controls, not @fluentui/react v8.
fluentAppliesBySurface.fluent2Meaning: Modern controls = Fluent 2 / Fluent UI React v9, applied via App.Theme.
fluentAppliesBySurface.guidanceToday: Say plainly: classic is not Fluent v8 React. Best you can do is a #0078d4-seeded modern theme.

fluentAppliesBySurface.surface: Power Apps - Teams canvas / MDA custom pages 'Fluent UI (v8) controls'
fluentAppliesBySurface.fluent1Meaning: Genuinely Fluent 1: controls literally named 'Fluent UI (v8) controls'.
fluentAppliesBySurface.guidanceToday: DEPRECATED. Only in Teams canvas apps and MDA custom pages. Advise upgrade, not new builds.

fluentAppliesBySurface.fluent1Meaning: Not selectable. Legacy classic look is gone; classic theme customizations no longer honored.
fluentAppliesBySurface.fluent2Meaning: New Look (Wave 1, GA) plus header/navigation refresh (Wave 2, preview).
fluentAppliesBySurface.guidanceToday: New Look is mandatory as of 2026 Wave 1 and makers cannot revert. Fluent 1 has no valid answer here.

fluentAppliesBySurface.fluent1Meaning: Officially supported: platform-library Fluent 8.29.0 or 8.121.1 with React 16.14.0.
fluentAppliesBySurface.guidanceToday: This is the one surface where Fluent 1 genuinely matters. Emit exact XML plus createV8Theme bridging.

fluentAppliesBySurface.fluent1Meaning: Nothing. Power Pages has never shipped Fluent React. It is Bootstrap 3.3.x or 5.
fluentAppliesBySurface.fluent2Meaning: Nothing shipped. Fluent 2 only as hand-authored CSS tokens.
fluentAppliesBySurface.guidanceToday: Style via Styling workspace then custom CSS. Microsoft warns against replacing Bootstrap.
